GraalVM Python setuptools ReDoS vulnerability. setuptools is bundled as a transitive dependency within GraalVM Python extensions but its package management functions are never invoked at runtime. This CVE requires setuptools to parse HTML during package lookup; no package lookups occur since all packages are pre-installed at build time via Maven graalpy-maven-plugin.

Stack exhaustion DoS in json-smart via unlimited recursive parsing of deeply nested JSON arrays and objects. Requires parsing attacker-controlled untrusted JSON input. Liquibase is a CLI tool that only processes JSON from local operator-controlled configuration files and database metadata. No network-facing JSON parsing surface exists.

statements.status_notes: Apache Tomcat RCE via Default Servlet partial PUT — file fragments uploaded to predictable temp paths trigger deserialization of assembled content. Also enables reading security-sensitive files.

Requires an HTTP PUT request to a running Tomcat servlet container with partial PUT enabled. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts the Tomcat HTTP server, never deploys any servlet, and never opens any network port. The Default Servlet, partial PUT handling, and file session persistence code paths are never activated.

Netty SslHandler resource exhaustion vulnerability via SSLEngine. This is a server-side vulnerability requiring an attacker to send malicious SSL/TLS data to a Netty server. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run a TLS server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections.

Spring Framework annotation resolution bypass in generic type hierarchies affecting @EnableMethodSecurity. Requires a running Spring application with method-level security annotations on generic type hierarchies. Liquibase is a CLI tool that does not use Spring Security, does not enable @EnableMethodSecurity, and does not start a Spring application context. The spring-core artifact is a transitive dependency.

Denial of service via HTTP/2 stream reset memory leak in Tomcat. Requires an HTTP/2 connection to a running Tomcat server. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server, never enables HTTP/2, and accepts no inbound network connections.

PostgreSQL JDBC driver channel binding bypass. The vulnerability only triggers when the JDBC connection property channelBinding is explicitly set to "require" (default is "prefer"). Liquibase does not configure channelBinding=require in any default configuration. The vulnerable enforcement code path in ConnectionFactoryImpl.doAuthentication() is not reachable under Liquibase's default configuration.

Denial of service via integer overflow in Tomcat multipart upload file size limit validation. Requires sending a crafted multipart HTTP upload to a running Tomcat server. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server and never processes inbound HTTP requests or multipart uploads.

Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server, never configures the Rewrite Valve, and never accepts HTTP requests.

statements.status_notes: Jackson Core 3.x maxNestingDepth constraint bypass in multiple parser implementations, enabling DoS via StackOverflowError from deeply nested JSON input.
statements.impact_statement: Nesting depth constraint bypass in Jackson Core 3.x UTF8DataInputJsonParser and ReaderBasedJsonParser. maxNestingDepth from StreamReadConstraints is not enforced, allowing a deeply nested JSON document to cause StackOverflowError. Liquibase is a CLI tool that only parses JSON from trusted, operator-controlled configuration files and changelog artifacts. It does not expose any JSON parsing endpoint to remote or untrusted input. As established in the prior assessment of GHSA-2m67-wjpj-xhg9, Liquibase does not rely on StreamReadConstraints as a security boundary.

TLS 1.3 cipher suite preference order not preserved in Tomcat's SSL connector configuration. Requires an active TLS connector performing cipher negotiation. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server or binds a TLS connector. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; no TLS handshakes occur.

statements.status_notes: Apache Tomcat authentication bypass where OCSP validation soft-fails even when soft-fail is explicitly disabled, allowing revoked client certificates to authenticate.
statements.impact_statement: Authentication bypass due to CLIENT_CERT soft fail misconfiguration in Tomcat's OCSP validation. Requires an active HTTPS connector configured with CLIENT_CERT authentication and an OCSP responder. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that uses picocli for command-line parsing and never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No connector, no authenticator, no OCSP — the code is inert.

Information disclosure via padding oracle vulnerability in Tomcat EncryptInterceptor (clustering component). Requires Tomcat clustering with EncryptInterceptor enabled. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server or initializes clustering. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; EncryptInterceptor is never instantiated.

Go stdlib crypto/x509 DoS vulnerability (GO-2026-4947). Detected in the compiled lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) binary built with Go 1.25.8. govulncheck symbol-level analysis confirms the vulnerable code paths are not called by lpm. Fix: DAT-22804 bumps Go to 1.25.9 in liquibase-package-manager, eliminating the vulnerability at the source.

statements.status_notes: Validating certificate chains which use policies is unexpectedly inefficient when certificates in the chain contain a very large number of policy mappings, possibly causing denial of service. This only affects validation of otherwise trusted certificate chains, issued by a root CA in the VerifyOptions.Roots CertPool, or in the system certificate pool.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib crypto/x509 certificate policy mapping DoS vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.9 and 1.26.2. Current Docker builds install lpm 0.3.3 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.3 declares go 1.25.9 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix.

Go stdlib internal/syscall/unix Root.Chmod symlink traversal vulnerability. Detected in the compiled lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) binary built with Go 1.25.8. govulncheck symbol-level analysis confirms the vulnerable code paths are not called by lpm. Fix: DAT-22804 bumps Go to 1.25.9 in liquibase-package-manager, eliminating the vulnerability at the source.

statements.status_notes: If one side of the TLS connection sends multiple key update messages post-handshake in a single record, the connection can deadlock, causing uncontrolled consumption of resources. This can lead to a denial of service. This only affects TLS 1.3.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib crypto/tls TLS 1.3 key update DoS vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.9 and 1.26.2. Current Docker builds install lpm 0.3.3 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.3 declares go 1.25.9 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix.

statements.status_notes: When using LookupCNAME with the cgo DNS resolver, a very long CNAME response can trigger a double-free of C memory and a crash.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib LookupCNAME double-free in the cgo DNS resolver when processing a very long CNAME response. lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image; it downloads Liquibase extension driver JARs from GitHub release assets via HTTP. lpm never calls LookupCNAME — standard HTTP hostname resolution uses LookupIPAddr/LookupHost, not the CNAME-specific API. Additionally, the vulnerability requires the cgo DNS resolver, which is not the default on Linux; the pure-Go DNS resolver is active in the eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble container.

statements.status_notes: When processing HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames, transport will enter an infinite loop of writing CONTINUATION frames if it receives a SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with a value of 0.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib HTTP/2 transport infinite loop when a server sends SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with a value of 0. lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image; it makes HTTP/2 connections to GitHub release servers to download Liquibase extension driver JARs. Exploitation requires a server to send the malformed SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE=0 frame. lpm only connects to trusted GitHub release CDN endpoints (URLs and checksums fixed in docker/Dockerfile:35-55); no attacker- controlled server endpoint exists in lpm's execution path.

statements.status_notes: Netty HttpObjectDecoder incorrectly terminates chunk header parsing at \r\n inside quoted strings in chunked transfer encoding extensions, enabling HTTP request smuggling.
statements.impact_statement: HTTP request smuggling via chunked transfer encoding in Netty HTTP codec. This is a server-side vulnerability requiring an attacker to send malicious HTTP/1.1 requests to a Netty HTTP server. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run an HTTP server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections. There is no listening socket for an attacker to exploit.

statements.status_notes: See CVE-2026-33870 entry on netty-codec-http. Mirrored here so scanners that flag netty-transport receive the same not_affected statement.
statements.impact_statement: Scanner over-match: the vulnerable code lives in netty-codec-http (see the sibling assessment above). OWASP Dependency-Check and similar CPE-based scanners propagate the CVE onto netty-transport via the broad cpe:2.3:a:netty:netty:* match. netty-transport ships no HTTP/1.1 chunked decoder, so even if it were exposed as a server (which Liquibase is not), the affected code path would not run from this artifact.

statements.status_notes: See CVE-2026-33870 entry on netty-codec-http. Mirrored for sibling transport artifact so scanners receive the same not_affected statement.
statements.impact_statement: Scanner over-match: same root assessment as netty-codec-http (see above). netty-transport-classes-epoll provides Linux epoll(7) native transport classes — no HTTP parser code. The cpe:2.3:a:netty:netty:* CPE causes OWASP to propagate the CVE here. Liquibase does not expose any HTTP server; the vulnerable chunked-encoding decoder is unreachable from this artifact regardless.

statements.status_notes: See CVE-2026-33870 entry on netty-codec-http. Mirrored for sibling transport artifact so scanners receive the same not_affected statement.
statements.impact_statement: Scanner over-match: same root assessment as netty-codec-http (see above). netty-transport-classes-kqueue provides macOS/BSD kqueue(2) native transport classes — no HTTP parser code. CPE-based propagation only.

statements.status_notes: Netty verifyContinuationFrame fails to limit the number of zero-byte CONTINUATION frames, bypassing maxHeaderListSize and causing excessive CPU consumption on the server.

This is a server-side vulnerability requiring an attacker to send malicious HTTP/2 CONTINUATION frames to a Netty HTTP/2 server. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run an HTTP/2 server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport. There is no inbound HTTP/2 listener.

statements.status_notes: See CVE-2026-33871 entry on netty-codec-http2. Mirrored for sibling transport artifact.
statements.impact_statement: Scanner over-match: same root assessment as netty-codec-http2 (see above). netty-transport-classes-epoll is the Linux epoll native transport — no HTTP/2 frame decoder. CPE-based scanners propagate the CVE here despite the artifact not containing the vulnerable parser.

Information disclosure via improper encoding in Tomcat JsonAccessLogValve. Requires an active HTTP connector with JsonAccessLogValve configured and non-default relaxedPathChars/relaxedQueryChars values. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; no access log valves are configured or initialized.

Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server or initializes clustering. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; Kubernetes cluster membership is never initialized.

statements.status_notes: Well-crafted inputs reaching ParseAddress, ParseAddressList, and ParseDate were able to trigger excessive CPU exhaustion and memory allocations.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib net/mail CPU exhaustion via pathological inputs to ParseAddress, ParseAddressList, and ParseDate. lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image. lpm is a package manager for Liquibase extension drivers and has no email processing functionality. The vulnerable net/mail parsing functions are not called by lpm at any point during package installation or management operations.

statements.status_notes: The Dial and LookupPort functions panic on Windows when provided with an input containing a NUL (0).
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib Dial and LookupPort panic vulnerability requires Windows when processing input containing a NUL byte. The assessed Liquibase Secure Docker image uses the Linux base image eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (docker/Dockerfile:2), so the vulnerable Windows runtime environment is absent.

statements.status_notes: XML External Entity (XXE) via Unsanitized Dictionary Parsing in Apache OpenNLP DictionaryEntryPersistor. Versions before 2.5.9 and before 3.0.0-M3 initialize dictionary XML parsing without secure processing or DTD restrictions, allowing attacker-supplied dictionary files to trigger local file disclosure or server-side request forgery during SAX parsing.
statements.impact_statement: OpenNLP DictionaryEntryPersistor XXE vulnerability fixed in 2.5.9. Liquibase Secure declares opennlp-tools through opennlp.version 2.5.8 (tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/pom.xml:76) in the phileas AI services dependency (tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/pom.xml:18, tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/pom.xml:19, tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/pom.xml:20), but the vulnerable dictionary XML parsing API is not imported or called. The only production OpenNLP usage found is document categorization and tokenization (tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/src/main/java/ai/philterd/phileas/service/ai/sentiment/OpenNLPSentimentDetector.java:22, tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/src/main/java/ai/philterd/phileas/service/ai/sentiment/OpenNLPSentimentDetector.java:23, tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/src/main/java/ai/philterd/phileas/service/ai/sentiment/OpenNLPSentimentDetector.java:24).

statements.status_notes: A local attacker on the same host as the application may be able to take control of the directory used by ApplicationTemp. When server.servlet.session.persistent is set to true and the attack persists across application restarts, this may allow the attacker to read session information and hijack authenticated users or deploy a gadget chain and execute code as the application's user.
statements.impact_statement: Spring Boot ApplicationTemp exploitation requires server.servlet.session.persistent=true and persistence across application restarts. Liquibase Secure's Docker image starts the Liquibase CLI entrypoint (docker/Dockerfile:68), and grep for server.servlet.session.persistent, ApplicationTemp, persistent=true, and setPersistent across Java, XML, properties, YAML, and YML files returned no matches.

statements.status_notes: In certain circumstances, Spring Boot's default web security is ineffective allowing unauthorized access to all endpoints. For an application to be vulnerable, it must be a servlet-based web application, have no Spring Security configuration of its own and rely on the default web security filter chain, depend on spring-boot-actuator-autoconfigure, and not depend on spring-boot-health.
statements.impact_statement: Spring Boot default web security bypass requires the application to depend on spring-boot-actuator-autoconfigure and not depend on spring-boot-health. The repository's Spring Boot declarations are spring-boot-autoconfigure provided for Pro integration (pro/pom.xml:78) and spring-boot-starter-web in the license utility (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:44); grep for spring-boot-actuator-autoconfigure, spring-boot-starter-actuator, and spring-boot-health across pom.xml files returned no matches.

statements.status_notes: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Apache Tomcat. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117. Older, unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version [FIXED_VERSION], which fixes the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Unbounded request body reads in Tomcat WebDAV LOCK and PROPFIND handling affect Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. The license utility pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.21 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26, tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:52) through spring-boot-starter-web (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:60) and starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20), but no WebDAV servlet, WebDAV mapping, or PROPFIND/LOCK handler is configured in tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main or its application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1).

statements.status_notes: Improper Input Validation vulnerability in Apache Tomcat: HTTP/2 request headers were not validated, which may have triggered unexpected application behavior. Affects Apache Tomcat 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, and 10.0.0-M1 through 10.0.27. Fixed in 11.0.22, 10.1.55, and 9.0.118.
statements.impact_statement: HTTP/2 request header validation gap in Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. Exploitation requires HTTP/2 connections to a running Tomcat server. Only the license utility includes tomcat-embed-core (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:49-52); it starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20) but does not enable HTTP/2 — application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1) sets no server.http2.enabled property and declares no HTTP/2 connector, and the codebase contains no HTTP/2-specific Tomcat configuration. The utility also pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26), so the fixed version is installed regardless.

statements.status_notes: Apache OpenNLP ExtensionLoader is vulnerable to arbitrary class instantiation via attacker-controlled input passed to the extension loading mechanism, potentially allowing remote code execution.
statements.impact_statement: Apache OpenNLP ExtensionLoader arbitrary class instantiation vulnerability. The ExtensionLoader API is not imported or called anywhere in Liquibase Secure. The only production OpenNLP usage is document categorization and tokenization via DoccatModel, DocumentCategorizerME, and WhitespaceTokenizer in OpenNLPSentimentDetector.java; no extension loading or dynamic class instantiation occurs.

statements.status_notes: pgjdbc is an open source postgresql JDBC Driver. From version 42.2.0 to before version 42.7.11, pgjdbc is vulnerable to a client-side denial of service during SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication. A malicious server can instruct the driver to perform SCRAM authentication with a very large iteration count.
statements.impact_statement: pgjdbc client-side SCRAM-SHA-256 denial-of-service is fixed in 42.7.11. The current source sets postgresql.version to 42.7.11 (pom.xml:55), and the distribution dependency uses that managed version (dist/pom.xml:117). The fixed version is therefore present in the current Liquibase Secure build source even though the scanner reported 42.7.9 for this image.

statements.status_notes: pgjdbc is an open source postgresql JDBC Driver. From version 42.2.0 to before version 42.7.11, pgjdbc is vulnerable to a client-side denial of service during SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication. A malicious server can instruct the driver to perform SCRAM authentication with a very large iteration count. With a large enough value, the client spends an unbounded amount of CPU time inside PBKDF2 before authentication can fail. A single attempt ties up a CPU core. Repeated or concurrent attempts exhaust client CPU and can wedge connection pools. In affected versions, loginTimeout did not fully mitigate this problem. When loginTimeout expired, the caller could stop waiting, but the worker thread performing the connection attempt could continue running and burning CPU inside the SCRAM PBKDF2 computation. This issue has been patched in version 42.7.11.
statements.impact_statement: PostgreSQL JDBC SCRAM-SHA-256 client-side denial of service fixed in 42.7.11. Liquibase Secure distribution declares postgresql.version as 42.7.11 (dist/pom.xml:23) and uses that property for the org.postgresql:postgresql dependency (dist/pom.xml:115, dist/pom.xml:117), so the vulnerable 42.7.9 code reported by the scanner is not present in the current distribution build.

statements.status_notes: Apache OpenNLP AbstractModelReader allocates unbounded memory when reading model files, allowing a malicious or malformed model file to cause an out-of-memory denial of service.
statements.impact_statement: Apache OpenNLP AbstractModelReader OOM denial-of-service vulnerability via unbounded memory allocation during model loading. Exploitation requires loading an attacker-controlled or malformed model file. Liquibase Secure bundles pre-packaged, trusted OpenNLP model files at build time; no model files are loaded from external or user-controlled sources at runtime. AbstractModelReader is not imported or called directly in Liquibase code.

statements.status_notes: Exposure of HTTP Authentication Header to unexpected hosts during WebSocket authentication in Apache Tomcat. Affects Apache Tomcat 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, 9.0.2 through 9.0.117, 8.5.24 through 8.5.100, and 7.0.83 through 7.0.109. Fixed in 11.0.22, 10.1.55, and 9.0.118.
statements.impact_statement: Exposure of HTTP authentication headers to unexpected hosts during WebSocket authentication in Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. Exploitation requires a WebSocket client following an HTTP redirect during authentication. Only the license utility includes tomcat-embed-core (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:49-52); it starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20) but does not use the Tomcat WebSocket client or server APIs. Application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1) contains no WebSocket endpoint definitions, and the codebase contains no ClientEndpoint/ServerEndpoint annotations or other WebSocket-related symbols. The utility also pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26).

statements.status_notes: Pathological inputs could cause DoS through consumePhrase when parsing an email address according to RFC 5322.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib net/mail DoS via pathological email address inputs reaching the consumePhrase parser (RFC 5322 phrase parsing). lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image. lpm is a package manager for Liquibase extension drivers and has no email processing functionality. The vulnerable net/mail consumePhrase code path is not reachable from any lpm operation.

Netty epoll native transport vulnerability fixed in 4.2.13.Final. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run any network server. netty-transport-native-epoll provides the Linux epoll(7) native transport for outbound client connections. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport. There is no inbound socket for an attacker to exploit.

statements.status_notes: Authentication Bypass Issues vulnerability in digest authentication in Apache Tomcat. Affects Apache Tomcat 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, and 8.5.0 through 8.5.100. Fixed in 11.0.22, 10.1.55, and 9.0.118.
statements.impact_statement: Authentication bypass in Tomcat digest authentication, where any unknown user presenting the password "null" was authenticated. Affects Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. Exploitation requires Tomcat to be configured to use DigestAuthenticator. Only the license utility includes tomcat-embed-core (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:49-52); it starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20) but does not configure any Tomcat realm or authenticator. Application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1) contains no realm/authenticator definitions, and the codebase contains no DigestAuthenticator or related symbols. The utility also pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26).

statements.status_notes: Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity in LockOutRealm in Apache Tomcat. Affects Apache Tomcat 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, and 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Fixed in 11.0.22, 10.1.55, and 9.0.118.
statements.impact_statement: LockOutRealm treats user names as case-sensitive, reducing its effectiveness against brute-force attacks. Affects Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. Exploitation requires Tomcat to be configured to use LockOutRealm. Only the license utility includes tomcat-embed-core (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:49-52); it starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20) but does not configure any Tomcat realm. Application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1) contains no realm definitions, and the codebase contains no LockOutRealm or related symbols. The utility also pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26).

statements.status_notes:
Improper Authorization vulnerability when multiple method constraints define an HTTP method for the same extension in Apache Tomcat.
This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.22, 10.1.55 or 9.0.118 which fix the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Apache Tomcat improper authorization vulnerability fixed in 11.0.22. Liquibase Secure pins tomcat-embed-core through tomcat.version 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26), and the dependency uses that property (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:52). The fixed version is therefore present and the vulnerable 11.0.21 code is not.

urllib3 vulnerability. urllib3 is bundled as a transitive dependency within GraalVM Python extensions but its HTTP client functionality is never invoked at runtime. All Python packages are pre-installed at build time via Maven graalpy-maven-plugin; no HTTP requests are made via Python at runtime.

statements.status_notes:
Covert timing channel vulnerability in Legion of the Bouncy Castle Inc. BC-JAVA core on all (core modules). This vulnerability is associated with program files FrodoEngine.Java.
This issue affects BC-JAVA: from 1.71 before 1.84.
statements.impact_statement: Bouncy Castle BC-JAVA FrodoEngine covert timing channel affects versions 1.71 before 1.84. Liquibase Secure distribution includes org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on:1.78.1 (core/liquibase-dist/src/main/archive/licenses/commercial/README.txt:1318), but grep for FrodoEngine, Frodo, org.bouncycastle.pqc, pqc.crypto.frodo, and BCPQC across Java sources returned no matches, so the vulnerable Frodo post-quantum cryptography code path is not reachable.

statements.status_notes: Jackson Core 3.x StreamReadConstraints.maxDocumentLength check can be bypassed in multiple code paths, weakening DoS protection for applications that rely on it.
statements.impact_statement: Document length constraint bypass in Jackson Core 3.x. The StreamReadConstraints.maxDocumentLength check can be bypassed in blocking parsers, async parsers, and DataInput path. jackson-core 3.x is a transitive dependency from Spring Boot 4.0.3 in liquibase-license-utility. Liquibase does not set maxDocumentLength (zero usages in codebase), does not process untrusted JSON input from external sources, and is a CLI tool — not a network-facing service. The constraint bypass only matters if relied upon for DoS protection, which Liquibase does not.
